title: Compliance, Budget, and SLA Decision Workshop
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Cobalt through proposed commercial path: MSA/DPA redline expectations, SSO/KMS options for Private deployment, SLA tiers for Dedicated, and pricing model tradeoffs. Legal raised egress and audit log questions; procurement pushed for 60 day pricing approval window and clause around data residency. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share final MSA redline, DPA mapping table, Dedicated SLA exhibit, cost scenarios spreadsheet, and schedule security follow-up/baseline test window.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share MSA draft with RAG'd redlines and a DPA mapping table; due 2026-07-23
Liam O'Connor: Provide Dedicated SLA exhibit and sample latency SLOs + rollback policy; due 2026-07-22
Eve Park: Send cost-scenarios spreadsheet (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with token math for their baseline workloads; due 2026-07-24
Daniel Wu / Redwood SE follow-up: Schedule security deep dive (KMS/HSM and on-prem packaging) week of 2026-07-27
next_steps: Redwood to email consolidated redlines and pricing scenarios
Cobalt legal to send priority MSA items inline (SLA credits, indemnity, data location)
Security deep dive to validate KMS and SOC 2 artifacts
Procurement to lock internal approval window: target decision by 2026-08-19
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-20 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~53 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Eve (Redwood) — Raj, Sofia, Daniel, Aisha (Cobalt)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda: commercial path, legal redlines, SLAs, and a security follow-up plan. we want to make sure procurement and legal have what they need to move to approval.

[00:18] Raj Patel: yeah thanks, Maya. timeline wise procurement's aiming to get vendor sign-off in august but legal needs a clean run through of MSA + DPA specifics. also cost number variance is a blocker.

[00:32] Aisha Khan: to call out — finance said we need a 60 day window to approve pricing at current TCO. after that we'll need re-approval.

[00:45] Maya Chen: got it. we'll include dated cost scenarios. Liam, want to take the SLA exhibit part?

[00:50] Liam O'Connor: sure. I'll pull up the Dedicated SLA exhibit — basically three tiers, 99.9, 99.95, 99.99 with associated credits and a defined rollback/fallback policy to a compatible model variant. note: the 99.99 tier has a coupling to reserved capacity commitments.

[01:12] Sofia Martinez: when you say rollback, does that mean our customer traffic could be routed to an external region or to a different model version? we need the definition spelled out for auditing.

[01:26] Liam O'Connor: yes — policy-based routing. normally fallback is to a variant we both approve; for private deployments we can do local fallback with on-prem packaged runtime. i will put explicit language showing region and model-variant constraints.

[01:45] Daniel Wu: security question — KMS: do you support customer-managed keys in the private bundle or only in the VPC flow with cloud KMS?

[01:59] Maya Chen: we support both. for Private (on-prem) we integrate with HSM/KMS connectors and you can bring keys; for VPC-option we integrate with major cloud KMS providers. i'll ask Liam to enumerate HSM vendors we test with.

[02:15] Liam O'Connor: yeah we have an HSM connector pattern and a KMS abstraction. i'll send a one-pager of supported HSMs and the key rotation cadence. note: encryption-at-rest and audit logs are part of the Private package but there are egress considerations if you want model updates.

[02:38] Sofia Martinez: egress — that's my next flag. we need clarity on data flows and whether any customer content leaves the region. also: do you offer contractual language for data residency?

[02:50] Maya Chen: absolutely. our DPA has language options: region-restricted processing, plus an exhibit mapping where keys and logs stay. we'll produce a DPA mapping table that shows controls and retention buckets.

[03:07] Aisha Khan: on pricing — what's the delta between hosted API and dedicated? we need clear per-token math for our expected throughput, and forecasting for spikes.

[03:20] Eve Park: i'll put numbers in the spreadsheet but high level: hosted is pay-as-you-go at a per-token rate, dedicated is committed capacity with a lower per-token amortized cost plus a monthly reservation fee. there's also a caching/kv approach to reduce token usage for repeated prompts.

[03:44] Raj Patel: caching — we've seen token savings differ a lot depending on prompt structure. can you show an example for our 6k seq use case?

[03:57] Liam O'Connor: yes. we can run a small benchmark during the pilot window — measure prefix caching and KV cache hit rates. that'll feed the cost model. we'll need a sample prompt set.

[04:14] Raj Patel: we can provision that. we'll share a representative traffic sample.

[04:22] Sofia Martinez: indemnity and limitation of liability — we have a pretty standard list but want to confirm Redwood's position on consequential damages and carveouts for third-party IP claims.

[04:36] Maya Chen: understood. on indemnity we'll align to standard SaaS market forms; we'll flag any customer-data or IP carveouts for review. i'll push a redline that highlights where we can be flexible.

[04:50] Daniel Wu: do you have SOC 2 Type II and do you provide a security portal with the doc package?

[04:57] Liam O'Connor: yes SOC 2 Type II in our security pack. we can share the attestation and a standard security questionnaire. for on-prem customers we also provide architecture runbooks.

[05:10] Sofia Martinez: audit logs: we need retention for seven years for some lines of business — is that feasible?

[05:18] Maya Chen: seven years is outside our default, but we can offer extended retention as an add-on. i'll write up options and estimated cost.

[05:30] Aisha Khan: procurement — payment terms: typical 45 days, but finance wants a 60 day. can that be accepted?

[05:38] Maya Chen: we can accommodate 60 day net for enterprise contracts; i'll have legal note it in the MSA draft.

[05:46] Raj Patel: one other technical ask — we sometimes need deterministic model version pinning for compliance. is that supported?

[05:56] Liam O'Connor: yes you can pin models by version in Dedicated and Private. hosted API also supports version tags but with a compatibility window. i'll add model-pin language to the deploy exhibit.

[06:13] Sofia Martinez: fallback credits — can we get an example SLA credits table for downtime and degraded quality? we need that to quantify risk.

[06:24] Liam O'Connor: i'll include a table where credits are percentage-of-monthly-fee tiers tied to latency SLO breaches and an extended outage bucket.

[06:36] Daniel Wu: baseline benchmarking — we want to schedule a two-week pilot window where Redwood runs throughput and latency tests against our sample prompts. will Redwood host that or do we spin up a test environment?

[06:50] Maya Chen: we typically run a hybrid: Redwood hosts an initial bench in our hosted env to validate model behavior, then for Dedicated/Private we'll run a pre-prod deploy in a dedicated pool or on-prem slice. for your compliance requirements we can run both and share traces.

[07:08] Raj Patel: timeline to get results?

[07:12] Liam O'Connor: initial hosted bench in 5 business days after sample receipt; full Dedicated pilot in ~10 business days plus provisioning lead time.

[07:20] Aisha Khan: procurement wants a clear gating checklist to route from evaluation to signature. can you produce a short checklist we can attach to the PO?

[07:31] Eve Park: yes we'll produce an onboarding checklist with legal acceptances, security artifacts, and a final cost sign-off.

[07:40] Sofia Martinez: one more legal point — data subject requests and deletion: what is your standard SLA for deletion and for handing over customer data on termination?

[07:52] Maya Chen: standard is 30 days for complete data erasure from hosted, with options for immediate certs in Private. we'll note that in the DPA mapping.

[08:05] Raj Patel: ok this is helpful. can you enumerate which clauses you expect will be redlined from your side vs what you expect we'll ask?

[08:15] Maya Chen: sure. from Redwood side we'll propose limited changes: payment terms, extended retention costs, model pinning language in the deploy exhibit. we expect customer redlines around indemnity, egress, and data residency — those are typical.

[08:30] Sofia Martinez: on indemnity — we require an IP breach carveout for generated content. how do you treat model output liabilities?

[08:40] Liam O'Connor: model output liability is often scoped in the DPA and MSA; we typically accept a representations-and-warranties structure plus mutual indemnity for IP infringement claims tied to provided prompts. we'll run legal through specifics.

[08:55] Daniel Wu: give us the SOC 2 report and penetration testing summary. i'll want to follow up with a security checklist during the deep dive.

[09:05] Maya Chen: we'll attach SOC 2 and the pen test summary. i'll have Eve follow up with the security bundle link in email.

[09:14] Raj Patel: cool. let's talk escalation — if we hit a blocker in legal, who at Redwood will be our escalation contact?

[09:22] Maya Chen: i'm the AE and will coordinate; but legal escalation goes to our head of legal and I'll copy them on priority items. for technical blockers Liam and our solutions architect group will be the contact.

[09:35] Aisha Khan: procurement checkpoint — does Redwood accept customer audits on-site for Private deployments?

[09:45] Liam O'Connor: yes, subject to scope and scheduling; we have a third-party audit framework and on-site review playbooks. we'll surface typical lead times.

[09:57] Sofia Martinez: ok i think we have enough to proceed to the redline pass. please highlight must-haves in your MSA email so legal can triage quickly.

[10:08] Maya Chen: will do. recap of deliverables: MSA redline, DPA mapping table, Dedicated SLA exhibit, pricing scenarios, SOC2 + pen test, onboarding checklist, schedule security deep dive. any other asks?

[10:26] Raj Patel: add the benchmarking window dates and sample prompt instructions to the pilot plan.

[10:33] Liam O'Connor: noted. we'll propose window dates in the follow-up.

[10:40] Sofia Martinez: and please call out any non-standard legal terms you cannot accept outright so we can decide early.

[10:48] Maya Chen: absolutely. thanks everyone for the time. we'll get the packet over by Friday.

[10:55] Raj Patel: thanks all.

[11:00] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription has some OCR-like name swaps (redwood product spelled Redwood Dedicated and sometimes 'red wood') and occasional filler words left in. Shared artifacts referenced: MSA draft link (sent after): https://redwood.example.com/msas/cobalt-draft , DPA mapping spreadsheet (will be attached), Dedicated SLA exhibit (slide deck link to be shared).
